abstract: BACKGROUND: Preserved fertility is an important issue for testicular cancer (TC) survivors. OBJECTIVE: Our aim was to examine any difference regarding paternity and testicular function following two, three, or four cycles of cisplatin-based chemotherapy for TC. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: A national multicentre follow-up survey assessing morbidity among survivors of unilateral TC diagnosed from 1980 to 1994 was conducted during the period 1998 to 2002. Of the 1814 men invited, 1462 (80.6%) participated by responding to a mailed questionnaire and/or undergoing a clinical examination including laboratory assessments. The present study includes the 316 participants up to 65 yr of age treated with two to four cycles of standard cisplatin-based chemotherapy without additional treatment beyond surgery. MEASUREMENTS: Self-reported paternity following treatment for TC according to number of cycles was assessed among men who reported antegrade ejaculation and attempts at posttreatment conception (n=106). Kaplan-Meier analysis, log-rank test, and Cox regression were applied. Gonadal hormones (n=305-314) and sperm counts (n=71) by number of cycles were assessed by linear by linear association or Mann-Whitney tests. RESULTS AND LIMITATIONS: At median 12-yr follow-up, 80% (85 of 106) had succeeded in their attempts of achieving posttreatment paternity (two cycles: 100%; three: 83%; four: 76%; p=0.022). For all patients the 15-yr actuarial paternity rate was 85%. The association between posttreatment paternity and number of cycles remained significant in the multivariate analysis (p=0.032). High serum follicle-stimulating hormone values were more common with increasing number of cycles (p=0.037), but there were no differences in serum luteinising hormone, serum testosterone, or sperm counts. Few men treated with two cycles and a limited number of sperm samples are the main limitations of this study. CONCLUSIONS: The prospects of future paternity after two to four cycles of cisplatin-based chemotherapy are good, and our data suggest that the prospects improve with decreasing number of cycles.
abstract_ja: 目的：精巣がんの生存者において、シスプラチン併用化学療法を2～4コース受けた後の妊孕性（父親になること）と精巣機能を調べること。デザイン、設定、対象：1980～1994年に単側精巣がんと診断された生存者の追跡調査を、1998～2002年に全国多施設で実施した。招待された1814人のうち1462人（80.6%）が参加した（質問票の回答および臨床検査）。本研究は、65歳以下で、手術のみを超える追加治療を受けず、標準的なシスプラチン併用化学療法を2～4コース受けた316人を対象とした。測定項目：射精があり治療後に妊娠を試みた男性106人を対象に、治療後の父親となったかどうかを化学療法コース数別に自己報告で評価した。Kaplan-Meier解析、ログランク検定、Cox回帰を用いた。コース数別の性腺ホルモン（n=305～314）および精子数（n=71）を、線形-線形連関検定またはMann-WhitneyのU検定で評価した。結果と限界：中央値12年の追跡で、80%（106人中85人）が治療後に父親となることに成功した（2コース100%、3コース83%、4コース76%、p=0.022）。全例の15年累積父親率は85%。化学療法コース数と治療後の父親となる率の関連は多変量解析でも有意であった（p=0.032）。コース数が増えるほど血清FSH高値が多かったが（p=0.037）、LH、テストステロン、精子数に差はなかった。2コース群の人数が少ないこと、精子検体数が限られることが本研究の限界である。結論：2～4コースのシスプラチン併用化学療法後の将来の父親となる見通しは良好であり、コース数が少ないほど見通しが良くなることが示唆された。
